sourceEvidence.claim: Age-related changes in pharmacokinetics — the intro (standard doses → ↑ plasma concentrations; older patients often require reduced doses to prevent toxicity) plus all four ▘ bullets verbatim (Absorption mostly unaffected; Distribution ↓TBW/↑fat; Metabolism ↓hepatic mass and blood flow with phase I decreased and phase II relatively preserved; Excretion ↓renal mass and blood flow, ↓GFR)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Aging alters the passage of drugs through the body and standard doses can result in ↑ plasma
concentrations. Older patients often require reduced doses to prevent toxicity.
▘ Absorption—mostly unaffected.
▘ Distribution—↓ total body water (↓ Vd of hydrophilic drugs → ↑ concentration), ↑ total body fat
(↑ Vd of lipophilic drugs → ↑ half-life).
▘ Metabolism—↓ hepatic mass and blood flow → ↓ first-pass metabolism, ↓ hepatic clearance.
Phase I of drug metabolism is decreased; phase II is relatively preserved.
▘ Excretion—↓ renal mass and blood flow (↓ GFR) → ↓ renal clearance.
